children: {b:1.3 Quality and making good defects}

children.name: text
children: You must make good any defects in your Subcontract Works within the period stated in the Subcontract.

children.name: text
children: If you fail to comply with this obligation, then we are entitled to employ others to make good the defects and all charges reasonably incurred by us in employing others will be recoverable from you.

children.name: text
children: {b:1.4 Inspection of site}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor should ensure that he has inspected the Site prior to the award of the Subcontract to satisfy themselves as to the nature of the Site, the degree or working space available, the means of access to the Site and any restrictions these may have on the proposed method of working.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor shall be deemed to be fully acquainted with the Site and for the avoidance of doubt Quinn London shall have no liability arising out of, or in relation to any issues relating to the access to and condition of the Site unless additional instruction is provided by Quinn London during the duration of the Subcontract.

children.name: text
children: {b:1.5 Site Waste Management}

children.name: text
children: It is the responsibility of the Subcontractor to ensure their working environment is kept clear and tidy at all times and wherever possible, dust extractors/methods of suppression are to be employed throughout the Subcontract Works. It is the responsibility of the Subcontractor to collect deposit waste into designated bins/chutes/skips etc. in accordance with the procedures advised by QLL during the site induction.

children.name: text
children: If the Subcontractor fails to keep their work areas clear and tidy the Subcontractor will be issued a 'Corrective Action Notice'. Failure by the Subcontractor to take immediate action may result in QLL employing others and a contra-charge will be levied against the Subcontractor at a rate of no less than £300 per notice.

children: {b:1.7 Environmental and Quality Management systems}

children.name: text
children: We at Quinn London operate an Environmental management system certified to ISO 14001 and a Quality Management System certified to ISO9001 on all our construction sites. As a sub-contractor you should ensure that you are aware of our Environmental policy, quality policy and site safety requirements and ensure your working methods are in line with the expectations set out within them.

children.name: text
children: {b:1.8 Health and Safety on site}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor is deemed to have included within the Price and Period for Completion its adherence to the requirements set out within this document.

children.name: text
children: Failure to adhere to these requirements can lead to the ejection of individuals from the Site and continued failure will lead to the termination of the Subcontract.

children.name: text
children: Any and all costs associated with the ejection and any delay caused will be borne by the Subcontractor.

children.name: text
children: {b:1.9 Emergency Arrangements}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor shall provide arrangements and resources to deal with any reasonably foreseeable accident or emergency occurring on the Site.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor shall be responsible for the provision of First Aid facilities for his employees in line with common law and statutory obligations under the Health and Safety (First Aid) Regulations 1981 and maintaining accident records.

children.name: text
children: All incidents shall be promptly logged with the Quinn London site manager.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor is obligated to report all accidents and near misses to the Quinn London site manager.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor's emergency arrangements must be accepted by the Contractor's representative before works on the Site commence. These emergency arrangements must be in force at all times whilst the Subcontractor is working. A demonstration of these arrangements to prove adequacy will be required.

children.name: text
children: {b:1.10 Quality}

children.name: text
children: Where and to the extent that materials, products and workmanship are not fully detailed or specified they are to be:-

children.name: text
children: In accordance with the applicable law, Regulatory Requirements, applicable standards, including codes of practice, and

children.name: text
children: Products are to be new unless otherwise specified.

children.name: text
children: No substances or materials are used which have been declared deleterious in any publication of the Building Research Establishment, British Standards or codes of practice current at the time of incorporation of such substances and materials into the Subcontract Works.

children.name: text
children: Of a standard appropriate to the Subcontract Works and suitable for the functions stated in or reasonably to be inferred from the drawings, specification and all other documents appended to this document.

children.name: text
children: Takes all necessary precautions to prevent damage to the Subcontract Work from frost, rain and other hazards.

children.name: text
children: Inspects components and products carefully before fixing or using and rejects any which are defective.

children.name: text
children: Fixes or lays securely, accurately and in alignment.

children.name: text
children: Where not specified otherwise, selects fixing and jointing methods and types, sizes and spacings of fastenings in compliance with manufacturer's recommendations. Fastenings to comply with relevant British Standards.

children.name: text
children: Provides suitable, tight packings at screwed and bolted fixing points to take up tolerances and prevent distortion and does not over-tighten fixings.

children.name: text
children: Adjusts location and fixing of components and products so that joints which are to be finished with mortar or sealant or otherwise left open to view are even and regular.

children.name: text
children: Ensures that all moving parts operate properly and freely and does not cut, grind or plane prefinished components and products to remedy binding or poor fit without approval.

children.name: text
children: In accordance with relevant good industry practice.

children.name: text
children: {b:1.11 Protection of Products}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor:

children.name: text
children: Prevents over-stressing, distortion and any other type of physical damage to products.

children.name: text
children: Keeps products clean and free from contamination. Prevents staining, chipping, scratching or other disfigurement, particularly of products exposed to view in the finished work.

children.name: text
children: Keeps products dry and in a suitably low humidity atmosphere to prevent premature setting, moisture movement and similar defects. Where appropriate products are stored off the ground to allow free air movement around and between products.

children.name: text
children: Prevents excessively high or low temperatures and rapid changes of temperature in the products.

children.name: text
children: Protects products adequately from rain, damp, frost, sun and other elements as appropriate and ensures that products are at a suitable temperature and moisture content at time of use.

children.name: text
children: Ensures that sheds and covers are of ample size, in good weatherproof condition and well secured.

children.name: text
children: Keeps different types and grades of products separately and adequately identified.

children.name: text
children: So far as possible keeps products in their original wrappings, packings or containers, until immediately before they are used.

children.name: text
children: Wherever possible retains protective wrappings after fixing and until shortly before completion of the Subcontract Works.

children.name: text
children: Ensures that protective measures are fully compatible with and not prejudicial to the products/materials.

children.name: text
children: {b:General communication}

children.name: text
children: All communication relating to the scope of works and contract documentation should be in writing and sent to the QLL QS, and QLL Contracts Manager as a minimum.

children.name: text
children: Minutes will be taken during all meetings between Quinn London and the Subcontractor that will be issued and agreed by both parties.

children.name: text

children.name: text
children: Any change to the scope and the associated documentation enclosed within this document will be notified to the Subcontractor through the issue of a contract notice by the project QS or Contracts Manager. The Subcontractor should not accept verbal instructions without confirmation being provided in writing from both the project QS and Contracts Manager.

children.name: text
children: {b:1.13 Labour and Equipment Returns}

children.name: text
children: At the beginning of each week the Subcontractor submits to the project QS records showing, for the previous week:-

children.name: text
children: The number, name and description of all persons, including managers, engineers, craftsmen, designers, labourers and other persons employed on or in connection with the work. The timesheets shall detail daily tasks, hours, start times, finish times and total hours worked on and off Site.

children.name: text
children: The Quinn London site manager is required to sign all labour and equipment returns.

children.name: text
children: {b:1.14 General}

children.name: text
children: {WashFacilities}. The Subcontractor must clean down all vehicles and plant before it leaves Site to minimise road cleaning.

children.name: text
children: The Site is unguarded at night.

children.name: text
children: Regardless of the security measures in place and provided by the Contractor, the Subcontractor is responsible for the security of their own material, plant and tools and the contractor takes no liability for their theft or damage.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor does not advertise, make any press release or statement, publish or supply for publication any information, drawing or visual recording concerning the Subcontract Works or the Project and does not use the Site for the purpose of advertisement without the written consent of Quinn London.

children: {b:1.15 Commercial}

children.name: text
children: Claims, Applications and Invoices.

children.name: text
children: All claims for monies must be submitted in accordance with the timetable set out in the Subcontract Order.

children.name: text
children: All claims must be submitted as an 'application' in accordance with the Subcontract terms. Invoices will be rejected, and a credit note for the full value of the invoice requested before any claim can be certified.

children.name: text
children: All claims must give an elemental breakdown of the works in sums no greater than those shown in 'Pricing Schedule' and include a cumulative percentage claim (or quantity, as appropriate) against each item.

children.name: text
children: All claims must include a running, cumulative 'Estimated Final Account'.

children.name: text
children: All additions or omissions to the Price must be clearly defined, broken down and shown below the contract works under the heading 'Variations'.

children.name: text
children: All claims for variations must be accompanied by a signed instruction from both the project QS and the Contracts Manager.

children.name: text
children: Any discounts are to be taken on the net cumulative total; before retention, TAX/CIS etc.

children.name: text
children: It is the responsibility of the Subcontractor to ensure their insurances are current and that QLL have up-to-date copies on record.

children.name: text
children: It is the responsibility of the Subcontractor to sign and return all VAT returns on previous payments and return these to QLL.

children.name: text
children: All applications must include at least one copy in an editable format i.e. Excel.
